findings.reason: the node would find its test green on base, prove no guard, and leave the section's real repair (the raising path that costs 4,150 run-file reads) unmeasured.
findings.text: §28's done-when asserts "A new process calls `ledger.load` and makes no `_read_run` call. With one run file changed, it makes exactly one", and its negative control says "the same tests against a copy of the base tree fail both counts"; but on the base tree a current index is served from `_indexed_data`, which reads no run file when none changed and reads exactly the one changed file through `_read_run` (reckon/ledger.py:1292), so both counts hold before any repair and the declared control cannot fail — the counts measure the healthy-index path the base already satisfies, not the live defect §28's Why names (the per-file full scan at ledger.py:1411 that a fresh process pays when `_indexed_data` raises at :1287 or :1296)

findings.reason: the trimmed-offset requirement is a robustness clause whose omission does not send the node down a wrong path or change what the section asks for; adding a truncation arm to the same test would strengthen it without altering the plan's mechanism.
findings.text: §30's deliverable requires "A stream that was truncated or replaced is read again from the start", but its done-when tests only the append case (appending ten lines parses exactly ten) and never truncates or replaces a stream, so an offset cache that ignores a shrinking file passes the gate with the stated behaviour broken
